qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: Dacia brand design-to-cost engineering provides a genuine low-cost value proposition in entry-level European passenger cars. However, mass-market volume automotive manufacturing is fundamentally commoditized and capital-intensive. Multi-cycle Group ROIC has averaged ~2-3% (well below the 12% hurdle), with operating margins structurally constrained between 3% and 8%. Primary erosion threats: low-cost Chinese EV imports into Europe, stringent EU fleet emissions penalties, cyclical consumer demand, and execution complexity across its unbundled Horse (ICE) and Ampere (EV) divisions.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 3b (ROIC < 12% & pricing power, REJECT). Despite Dacia's low-cost design-to-cost discipline under the 'Renaulution' turnaround, Renault operates in the structurally commoditized European volume auto market. Multi-cycle Group ROIC averages just 2-3% (far below the 12% hurdle), with operating margins capped around 7-8%. Severe price competition from low-cost Chinese EV entrants and heavy powertrain transition capex destroy excess returns.
qualitative.evidence: Consolidated Group ROIC hovered between 0.9% and 3.0% from 2021 to 2024, failing the 12% hurdle across the cycle. Group operating margins stabilized at 7.6% in 2024 (€4.26B operating income on €56.2B revenue), but remain vulnerable to cyclical downshifts. High structural capital expenditures required for the EV transition, cancellation of the Ampere IPO, complex cross-shareholdings with Nissan, and intense pricing pressure from imported Chinese EVs in Europe prevent the generation of durable economic rents.
